subject: Eval coverage gap — action list & proposed A/B window
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Eval coverage gap — action list & proposed A/B window

Liam / team,

Thanks for the flag during the pilot call this morning — you were right: our current promptset only covers 62% of the product taxonomy examples you shared, and that gap risks a measurable quality delta in the first A/B cohort. I pulled a short matrix to highlight the missing classes (attached: eval_matrix_v2.xlsx) and sketched a minimal mitigation plan below.

Proposed immediate actions (week 0–2):
- Expand promptset with 12 targeted examples for the four missing categories (Marissa to own).
- Extend A/B test window by 3 business days for cohort 1 to gather extra signal for the low-frequency classes (Jonas to confirm infra impact).
- Add a hard acceptance gate on recall for the 4 categories (threshold: recall >= 70% across sampled prompts) before full rollout.
- Run a focused manual review of 150 responses from cohort A for coverage and hallucination (Sean to coordinate).

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-category recall documented in the matrix and meeting the threshold above.
- No increase in critical hallucinations (>1% by our definition) in the extended cohort.
- Product sign-off from Acme on coverage expansion examples.

Links: kanban/board (https://drive.re/redwood/acme-eval-board) — I created a quick backlog card and labeled the highest priority items.

Can Marissa and Jonas confirm owners + feasibility by EOD? Liam, we can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow if you prefer a live walkthrough.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Product Manager, Evals & Quality
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet summary of missing classes and example prompts)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmeretail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Eval coverage gap — action list & proposed A/B window

Irene — thanks for the matrix, that helped. Quick notes from my side after a first pass: 

- I can own prompt expansion. I'll draft the 12 targeted prompts and a small labeling guide by tomorrow noon PT. I'll include both positive and adversarial shots for each class (to stress hallucination).
- For acceptance criteria, suggest we add a secondary precision floor for the low-frequency classes (precision >= 60%) so we don't swing the model toward over-generation in pursuit of recall.
- For manual review, recommend a split: 100 targeted-class examples + 50 random samples to surface regressions. Sean, can you confirm reviewer availability?

Minor ask: if we extend the A/B window by 3 business days, we should lock the model variant we intend to promote to avoid confounding the signal. Jonas — can you confirm if we can pin the variant for the cohort?

If everyone agrees, I'll push the prompt draft to the Drive card and tag Liam for product confirmation.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead, Evals & Validation
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:40:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Eval coverage gap — action list & proposed A/B window

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 09:22 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Liam / team,
> 
> Thanks for the flag during the pilot call this morning — you were right: our current promptset only covers 62% of the product taxonomy examples you shared...

Quick infra update: pinning the cohort model variant is fine — we can create a cohort release that locks the model hash and disables rolling updates. The only impact is that autoscaling thresholds for that cohort will default to conservative limits for the first 48 hours; I estimate a ~7% cost delta for those days. If procurement needs to approve, we should surface that.

Attached a short timeline for the proposed A/B extension so teams can align on gating and monitoring (attachment: ab_timeline.png).

Alternative canary criteria suggestion: rather than an extension for all users, we could run the extra-signal window on a 20% subset of the cohort focused on the missing categories (routing by exposure). That reduces cost but requires a small routing rule and an updated experiment config. Trade-offs below: 
- Full-window extension: simpler to analyze, higher cost.
- Targeted subset: lower cost, slightly more complex to instrument but gives direct signal on the missing classes.

Happy to discuss on a quick call — Marissa, which option do you prefer from an eval purity perspective?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ab_timeline.png (visual test schedule and metric checkpoints)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 02:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Eval coverage gap — action list & proposed A/B window

Thanks all — clear plan. A few actionable decisions from my side: 

1) Reviewer pool: I can allocate two senior evaluators for the manual review next week; we'll follow Marissa's split (100 targeted / 50 random).
2) Canary approach: I prefer the targeted subset routing — it gives the cleanest signal on the categories without the full cost delta. Jonas, please open INF-1127 with the routing config and copy me.
3) Exception approval: I'm OK to sign off on a temporary extension/exception to the standard A/B window provided the following are true by the end of the extended window:
   - Per-category recall >= 70% AND precision >= 60% for the four classes.
   - No >1% critical hallucinations in the sampled set.
   - Acme product rep (Liam) provides written confirmation on coverage adequacy.

Liam — if that set of gates looks reasonable, can you confirm so procurement can be looped if needed? If yes, Marissa please tag the Drive doc when you push the prompts and I'll mark the exception approved internally.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
